Subject: Dedicated capacity options: initial sizing + ramp (CedarPoint Bio)

Emma —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As promised, attaching a concise set of reservation options tailored to the usage profile you shared (spikey inference for gen2 models, steady nightly batch embedding jobs). High-level options below; full breakdown attached (CPB_dedicated_options_v1.pdf) and a pricing model workbook.

Quick summary of the three proposal tiers:

- Starter lane (min 16 GPUs): low up-front commitment, supports burstable traffic and a small warm-standby for KV cache. Good for pilots and early production. Recommended ramp: 16 -> 32 within 60 days if 95th-percentile QPS grows >40%.

- Growth lane (min 64 GPUs): production baseline for the ML inference patterns you outlined. Includes 2x burst windows per month and baseline caching. Ramp: 64 -> 128 across 90 days, with auto-scale policy tied to token throughput.

- Enterprise lane (min 200 GPUs): reserved capacity + priority routing, SLA 99.9% and dedicated burst pool. Typical for cross-region HA and predictable volume. Ramp: staged (200 -> 400) across 120–180 days with staged warm-start credits.

Key configurable items we recommend selecting in the contract:
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs (floor) and burst pool size
- Warm-start credits (to pre-warm KV cache during activation windows)
- Step-up triggers (explicit QPS/token thresholds that start the next tranche)
- Fallback routing policy (if primary cluster saturated -> compatible smaller model variant)

Action items I propose:
1) You: confirm which lane aligns with your procurement appetite (Starter/Growth/Enterprise).
2) Procurement: provide preferred contract start date and any standard PO terms.
3) Us: send a tailored SOW + mutual action plan after we lock the lane and ramp timing.

Attaching: CPB_dedicated_options_v1.pdf, CPB_pricing_model_v1.xlsx

Talk soon — happy to hop on a follow-up to walk through the ramp triggers and warm-start economics.

Best,
Dev

Thanks, Dev — this is really helpful. A few clarifying questions before we loop in legal/procurement: 

1) For the Starter lane, can we have a guaranteed burst pool (e.g., extra 8 GPUs) for 4 peak windows/month? We need to avoid throttling during overnight processing for a 3rd-party partner.
2) What is the warm-start credit cadence? If we sign with a Sept 1 start date, do we get any free warm-start days to prime caches?
3) On the Growth lane, can you confirm the expected token-cost delta if we move from FP16 to an 8-bit quantized variant? Our infra team is sensitive to per-token spend.

Procurement, can you confirm whether CedarPoint prefers milestone invoicing or monthly invoices for a reserved capacity contract?

If possible, can we schedule a 30-minute call Wed to walk the options with Marissa?

Forwarding Emma's questions — quick recommendations from pricing/runtime: 

- Starter lane: make minimum 32 GPUs instead of 16 (we've seen large pilots burn through 16 with night batches + partner spikes). Offer a guaranteed burst pool of +8 GPUs for up to 4 peak windows per month as a configurable add-on.
- Warm-start credits: we can provide 10 warm-start days in the first 30 days for any lane signed in Q3 (applies to Sept 1 start). After that, credits are billable. Call out in SOW: 10 complimentary warm-start days if start_date <= 2026-09-30.
- Quantization delta: moving from FP16 to 8-bit typically reduces per-token GPU time ~30–40% depending on model family; we'll include concrete estimates in CPB_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (sheet: quantization_sensitivity).
- Ramp triggers: propose deterministic step triggers tied to 7-day moving average of token throughput (two consecutive days > threshold triggers next tranche). This avoids noisy single-day spikes.

I'll draft the small SOW appendix language for the warm-start credit and the burst windows. Also suggest we include a 45-day evaluation clause for early termination on Starter lane with prorated credits.

-M
